classification_rule:
Written because a summary assembled from memory is where selective reporting creeps in. Each
row names the artifact it came from, so any line can be checked, and the classification rule is
applied mechanically rather than by recollection:

rows.item: Unconditional harm reduction (B13)
rows.result: 28.2% undefended -> 10.4%; task-alone base rate 1/309
rows.caveat: population changed from the 42.3%->12.5% figure, so levels are not comparable

rows.item: Provenance reaches classes content-only cannot (pre-registered)
rows.result: additive fabrication 0/72 -> 37/72 (p=1e-11); fabricated preferences 0/48 -> 27/48 (p=1e-08); legitimate-instruction false flags 14/40 -> 2/40

rows.item: Provenance is cheaper than the stack it replaces
rows.result: B13 0.1s vs B12 0.15s per admitted memory

rows.item: Bespoke signals beat every published detector on memory poisoning
rows.result: own attacks: B13 46.1% vs deberta 14.1%; baselines 3-15% on note-shaped poisoning

rows.item: Our false-positive rates far below the baselines' on ordinary memory
rows.result: B13 1/1088, B15 1/1088 vs deberta 8/1088, Llama Guard 23/1088

rows.item: Working-set discipline (the round's main methodological contribution)
rows.result: 1117/2628 = 42.5% of instances both subvert an undefended agent and implement their label; per-population floors break CI on drift

rows.item: AgentPoison published records function once probed correctly
rows.result: 0/6 -> 3/6 working, task-alone base rate 0; four prior readings were measurement error

rows.item: memory_worm regeneration
rows.result: 33% mechanism-correct -> 90.0% by an out-of-loop judge; undefended harm 83.3% at 60% retrieval -> 3.3% with B13

rows.item: Corroboration fix lifts every founding family
rows.result: sleeper 0% -> 37%, MPBench 11% -> 46%, MINJA 13% -> 33%, DSRM 17% -> 30%, FARMA 74% -> 87%; aggregate own-attack recall 46.1% -> 59.7%, discrimination +46.1 -> +52.2
rows.caveat: costs 7.5% ordinary-benign FPR, all of it on untrusted channels

rows.item: Corroboration costs nothing on user-authored content
rows.result: legitimate standing instructions 0/40, named-party preferences 0/6, confirmed-human 0/20 in the user_turn channel with evidence live

rows.item: Union configurations beat both components at no extra FPR (descriptive)
rows.result: B17 own 51.2% vs B13 46.1% / B14 41.2%; adds no ordinary-benign false positive

rows.item: Matched operating points close most of the baseline gap
rows.result: deberta +36.9 vs B14 +34.1; was a 17-point gap at shipped thresholds, now 2.8
rows.caveat: the baseline still leads on that corpus

rows.item: Multi-hop is not a reasoning ceiling
rows.result: every agent 80-87% correct under the LLM judge; Gemini 60.0% strict, below phi3:mini's 65.0%; the oracle ceiling is NLI strictness
rows.caveat: this corrects a claim this project had published

rows.item: Three frozen hold-outs with pre-registration and digest verification
rows.result: 1,258 + 1,200 + 1,000 human-authored attacks; hold-out 3 adds 995 MATCHED benign from the same platforms

rows.item: Matched-benign false-positive rates are very high
rows.result: B18 54.9%, B14 54.5%, B13 33.5% against 0.09% on ordinary memory
rows.caveat: every FPR previously published used benign text unlike the attack distribution

rows.item: Three of five pre-registered predictions failed
rows.result: P2 (B18 beats B14 by 5pts) failed at +0.4; P4 (baselines degrade most) failed backwards; P5 (nothing above 85%) failed for four configs

rows.item: The recall ranking inverts once FPR is counted
rows.result: B14/B17/B18 reach 92.7-93.1% recall by flagging >half of benign; their discrimination is the worst of the configurations tested

rows.item: My labelling-artifact hypothesis was mostly wrong
rows.result: 82.7% of the corpus is benign-as-a-memory; filtering moves B18 only 54.9% -> 49.0%, about 6 of 55 points

rows.item: The content detector is the false-positive source, not provenance
rows.result: content-only 43.0% on DEV in-the-wild benign; corroboration adds 2 of 200
rows.caveat: my earlier reading blamed corroboration and was wrong

rows.item: 'B13 is the recommendation' was wrong unqualified
rows.result: on working attacks B14 STRICTLY dominates B13 on the clean hold-out, 40/64 vs 8/64, +32/-0, p=5e-10; B13's 12.5% there was unreported

rows.item: B14's hold-out gap is half composition, half inherited from deberta
rows.result: 36.6-point gap narrows to 20.6 on working attacks (p=0.0001); B14 agrees with deberta 90.1% on external corpora and degrades worse than it across corpora

rows.item: The union configurations are badly calibrated
rows.result: B17 leaves 6.2 and B18 9.2 points of discrimination on the table at their shipped thresholds

rows.item: The first pre-registered adaptive test was underpowered and I had to revise its design
rows.result: 1/38 vs 0/38 at p=1.0: one control event caps the p-value regardless of the true effect. Superseded by the powered re-run, but the original rule did fail

rows.item: Exfiltration regeneration only half worked
rows.result: 38% -> 68.8% out-of-loop, but generator acceptance 38.1% equals the unguided rate, so the spec did not improve authoring

rows.item: My own errors this round
rows.result: AgentPoison trigger error a 5th time (caught by my own new guard test); rejection-memory dev fit measured the wrong distribution; orphan script killed the pipeline runner; a guard test matched its own docstring; corroboration left inert in every published table; the user_turn arm computed but never reported; B12 omitted from the table testing it

rows.item: Five of seven founding families are weakly detected content-only
rows.result: DSRM, MPBench, MINJA, MemoryGraft 11-32%; sleeper 0% before the corroboration fix

rows.item: Adaptive evasion resolved (the open item of every prior round)
rows.result: 32/130 = 24.6% stateless control -> 1/130 = 0.8% with the ledger; paired +0/-31, p=9.31e-10 over 31 discordant pairs, 20 families
rows.caveat: radius was pre-registered but the SEED RULE was revised after the first test failed; and the 0.90 radius carries a 29.7% ledger-poisoning blast radius against 0.7% at 0.97, so the finding is the trade, not a solved problem

rows.item: Exfiltration is an UNTESTED mechanism
rows.result: 0/32 harm with a neutral task, provisioned store and recipient-aware judge; the poison names an outbound recipient in only 6/32 instances, so the generator failed its own specification and the mechanism judge passed them anyway
rows.caveat: four rival explanations eliminated by measurement; no detection or harm figure for this family is evidence about the attack class

rows.item: B17/B18 have no clean hold-out estimate
rows.result: both were chosen after reading hold-out results; hold-out 3 tested them once, and their shipped calibration is poor there

rows.item: All three hold-outs are injection/jailbreak corpora
rows.result: a good score there is evidence about overt injected instructions, not about additive fabrication or preference hijack; this project's own populations remain the only test of those

rows.item: Every phase verified end to end
rows.result: 3,466 tests passed, 32 skipped, 0 failed across phases 3-17, attribution and the cross-cutting suite; phase 3 and phase 5 datasets intact and needing no regeneration
